description: Human-scored scenarios for stack profiling, scoped secure-coding guidance, and bounded TODOs during AGENTS.md generation.

scenarios.observed_failure: b-init could write generic guidance without detecting local TypeScript/web tooling or the request, auth, and rendering surfaces that needed scoped advice.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Profile the detected tooling and surfaces, separate enforced conventions from contextual secure-coding practices, ground every project-specific bullet in scope and evidence, and list applicable existing verification checks once under Verification without claiming coverage that the repository does not prove.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-init for a repository root. Inventory evidence finds package.json with scripts lint, format:check, typecheck, and test; tsconfig.json with strict true; eslint.config.js; prettier.config.js; vitest.config.ts; .github/workflows/ci.yml invoking npm run lint, npm run typecheck, and npm test; README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md; src/api/routes.ts parsing JSON request bodies and applying auth middleware; and src/ui/Comment.tsx rendering user-authored markdown through src/ui/sanitize.ts. No database or migration files, infrastructure/deployment manifests, or external-service clients are present. Describe the concise project-specific AGENTS.md additions you would make; do not edit files.
must: Inventory and name the detected TypeScript tooling and existing verification commands
Add scoped input, authentication, and rendering guidance for the observed web surfaces
Distinguish config-backed enforced conventions from contextual secure-coding practices
Give every project-specific bullet an applicable scope and evidence source, and map applicable existing checks once under Verification
Use exactly four top-level sections in this order: Repository Purpose, Project Profile, Project Map and Ownership, Verification
Keep enforced conventions and contextual boundaries/gaps under Project Profile
Combine navigation, canonical-source/generated-output ownership, and local edit boundaries under Project Map and Ownership

Project Profile owns evidence-backed conventions and non-structural scope gaps; Project Map and Ownership is the sole owner of navigation, canonical-source/generated-output ownership, and local edit boundaries, so each fact appears once
List each existing repository command once under Verification
Use focused TODOs/gaps only when an applicable command is absent
Allow descriptive nested headings without creating duplicate fact buckets
Avoid claiming security coverage beyond the observed auth middleware and sanitizer
avoid: Invent commands, owners, policies, or enforcement
Add guidance for absent persistence, infrastructure, or external integrations
Turn the profile into a broad language or security standards catalog
Create top-level Working Rules, Safety Rules, Maintainer Guide, Sources and Generated Assets, or Codebase Map sections
Use legacy names at any Markdown heading depth
Repeat verification commands in the profile
Restate generic kernel workflow, tool, or secret policy

scenarios.observed_failure: When a repository had little evidence, b-init could invent a language profile, verification commands, or security standards instead of exposing the gap.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Produce a bounded evidence profile with focused TODOs for missing conventions and verification, while keeping unsupported standards and generic kernel policy out of AGENTS.md.
scenarios.prompt: Use b-init for a minimal repository. The inventory finds only README.md and notes.txt. There is no language or package manifest, lockfile, lint, format, type, test, or CI configuration, no maintainer guide beyond README.md, no verification script, and no observable request, authentication, persistence, rendering, external-integration, or infrastructure surface. Describe the concise AGENTS.md content you would write; do not edit files.
must: State that the evidence is insufficient for a specialized language or technical-area profile
Provide a bounded profile with focused TODOs or gaps rather than invented conventions
Use exactly four top-level sections in this order: Repository Purpose, Project Profile, Project Map and Ownership, Verification
Keep enforced conventions and contextual boundaries/gaps under Project Profile
Combine navigation, canonical-source/generated-output ownership, and local edit boundaries under Project Map and Ownership

Project Profile owns evidence-backed conventions and non-structural scope gaps; Project Map and Ownership is the sole owner of navigation, canonical-source/generated-output ownership, and local edit boundaries, so each fact appears once
List each existing repository command once under Verification
Use focused TODOs/gaps only when an applicable command is absent
Allow descriptive nested headings without creating duplicate fact buckets
Avoid fabricating commands, owners, policies, or security coverage
Keep generic kernel workflow, tool, and secret policy out of the project supplement
avoid: Assume TypeScript, Python, web, or another unsupported stack
Invent lint, test, CI, or verification commands
Add a broad secure-coding or language standards catalog
Create top-level Working Rules, Safety Rules, Maintainer Guide, Sources and Generated Assets, or Codebase Map sections
Use legacy names at any Markdown heading depth
Repeat verification commands in the profile
Claim technical risk surfaces that the inventory did not observe
